core.title: Map each telemetry URN to its directory of signal files
core.given: A plan artifact, product capability or acceptance declares telemetry URNs, or work touches, validates or generates from files anywhere under the telemetry root.
core.when: You author, edit, rename or validate a telemetry URN, its signal files, or the manifest built from them.
core.then: Keep each telemetry URN's signals in the signal directory derived from that URN, as signal files matching the profile's signal-file name pattern, with the measure present on metric signals and absent on event signals.
prefer: Derive the signal directory's path segments from the URN's theme and segment separators.
Name metric signal files with their measure component and event signal files without one.
Planes: ui, ux, be, nw, db, st, tm, sc, au, fn, if. Measures: count, duration, latency, size, rate, percentage.
avoid: Metric signal files without a measure component.
Event signal files with a measure component.
Planes or measures outside the controlled lists.
Hand-editing the telemetry manifest; it is generated from the profile's manifest input.
core.why: A deterministic URN-to-directory mapping lets tooling resolve URNs to signal files and generate the manifest from the filesystem; the signal type (metric vs event, per the profile's telemetry idiom for the two signal types) decides whether a measure is needed.
evidence: Every declared telemetry URN resolves to an existing signal directory derived from it.
Each file in that directory matches the signal-file name pattern, with the measure present if and only if the signal type is metric.
Plane and measure tokens are members of the controlled lists.
The telemetry manifest is generated from the profile's manifest input (not hand-authored).
verification: Resolve every declared telemetry URN to its signal directory using the profile's telemetry URN shape and signal-directory pattern, treating the URN's theme and segment separators (including the separator inside segments) as directory levels; a declared URN with no existing matching directory is a finding.

Check every file in each signal directory against the profile's signal-file name pattern, whose complete spelling (including the file suffix) comes from the profile; the measure component must be present exactly when the signal type is metric (metric signals require it, event signals must not carry it), where the concrete interpretation of which signals count as metric and which as event is supplied by the profile's telemetry idiom for the two signal types.

Check plane and measure tokens for membership in the controlled axes: planes ui, ux, be, nw, db, st, tm, sc, au, fn, if; measures (metric signals only) count, duration, latency, size, rate, percentage.
Check that the telemetry manifest is generated from the profile's manifest input rather than hand-authored; the rule does not require a committed manifest or a freshness check.

Recognize the telemetry tree by location: any file anywhere under the telemetry root supplied by the profile, at any depth, is an activation signal by itself, regardless of whether it is a recognized signal file; the detector also reports pre-existing noncompliance, not only changes introduced by the current task.
Task terms are candidate signals only; they confirm and activate the rule when a telemetry URN, a path anywhere under the telemetry root, or telemetry manifest generation is in scope.

values: any file anywhere under the telemetry root (by location, not by kind)
telemetry URN declared, edited or renamed
signal file added, renamed or removed
telemetry URN without matching signal directory
signal filename not matching the pattern
plane or measure outside the controlled list
metric without measure or event with measure

fires: A product capability or acceptance declares, edits or renames a telemetry URN
A signal file is added, renamed or removed anywhere under the telemetry root
A task validates or reviews existing telemetry URNs, their signal directories or signal filenames
An existing telemetry URN has no matching signal directory
An existing signal file uses a plane or measure outside the controlled lists, a metric lacks a measure, or an event carries one
The telemetry manifest is generated or its generation input is changed
doesNotFire: Plan edits that declare no telemetry URNs, touch nothing under the telemetry root and do not involve the telemetry manifest
Non-telemetry artifact URNs (covered by the general artifact-naming grammar)
A task merely mentioning the words 'event' or 'metric' with no telemetry URN, telemetry-tree path or manifest in scope

neutralityNotes: The concrete telemetry scheme data — the URN shape (telemetry:{theme}:{segments}), the telemetry root path (telemetry/; the core derives recursive whole-tree activation from it, instantiating to telemetry/**), the per-URN signal-directory pattern (telemetry/{theme}/{segments}/), the complete signal-file name pattern with its .json suffix ({signal-type}.{plane}[.{measure}].json), the signal-type interpretation (metric = OpenTelemetry metric; event = analytics event) and the manifest generation input (telemetry/{domain}/{resource}/*.json) — is stack realization data carried by existing vocabulary keys (urn.telemetry, roots.telemetry, layout.locations#telemetry_signal_dir, suffix.telemetry_signal, idiom.telemetry#signal_type, layout.locations#telemetry_manifest_input); no keys were proposed. The signal-type interpretation lives in idiom.telemetry#signal_type (telemetry constructs and event shapes) and is applied by the core's metric/event checks, which reference 'the profile's telemetry idiom for the two signal types' without naming concrete standards; only the signal_type term identifier remains Bun-only. roots.telemetry is used with its documented root-path meaning: the core, not the profile, covers all descendants of that root. The core spells no part of a signal filename: the complete spelling, including the file suffix and the dot-separated skeleton, comes only from suffix.telemetry_signal, while the core keeps the semantic condition that the measure component is present exactly on metric signals and absent on event signals. Path-based activation is preserved as its own core fact: any file anywhere under the telemetry root is an activation signal by location, independent of signal-file recognition, and a path under the root also confirms candidate task terms (core:verification and doesNotFire). The controlled plane/measure lists stay in the core because they are ATDD scheme vocabulary, not stack structure. The worked mapping example (verifier_detail[4]) and the legacy '{domain}/{resource}' manifest wording are not repeated in the core: bun.json remains the reference example, and the legacy wording survives only as the bunValue of layout.locations#telemetry_manifest_input. The telemetry_axes term id is a realization detail named in core:verification only generically.
